claims.claim: Retatrutide is a triple hormone receptor agonist targeting GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors currently in development for obesity treatment.
claims.quote: Retatrutide, a hormone receptor agonist targeting glucagon, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, is being developed to treat obesity.

claims.claim: Phase 2 trials for retatrutide have shown up to 24% body weight reduction in study participants.
claims.quote: Phase I proof-of-concept studies led to phase II trials showing up to 24% body weight reduction and nearly 20 cm waist circumference reduction.

claims.claim: Gastrointestinal adverse effects are the most commonly reported side effects associated with retatrutide treatment in clinical studies.
claims.quote: The most common adverse effects were gastrointestinal.

claims.claim: Effective pharmacological therapies for patients with MASH-related cirrhosis currently remain an unmet clinical need.
claims.quote: Despite recent advances, effective pharmacological therapy for MASH-related cirrhosis remains an unmet need, underscoring the importance of early identification and intervention.

claims.claim: In pre-clinical cancer models, retatrutide administration resulted in a 14-fold reduction in tumor volume in pancreatic cancer engraftment models.
claims.quote: pancreatic cancer engraftment was reduced, tumor onset was delayed, and progression was attenuated resulting in a 14-fold reduction in tumor volume compared to only 4-fold reduction in single agonist semaglutide-treated mice.

claims.claim: Retatrutide treatment in a lung cancer mouse model resulted in a 17-fold reduction in tumor volume compared to controls.
claims.quote: RETA-induced protection extends to a lung cancer model with 50% reduced tumor engraftment, significantly delayed tumor onset, and mitigated tumor progression, with a 17-fold reduction in tumor volume compared to controls.

claims.claim: In murine models, retatrutide effects are linked to the concurrent inhibition of PI3K-AKT and NF-κB pathways.
claims.quote: retatrutide effects with concurrent inhibition of both PI3K-AKT and NF-κB pathways.

claims.claim: Retatrutide increased the force of contraction in human right atrial preparations in an isolated tissue setting.
claims.quote: We noted that cumulatively applied retatrutide starting at 10 nM (up to 100 nM the highest concentration tested) elevated FOC in HAP in a concentration- and time-dependent manner.

claims.claim: The TRANSCEND-CKD study is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2b trial evaluating retatrutide in adults with obesity and chronic kidney disease.
claims.quote: TRANSCEND-CKD is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2b mechanistic study evaluating the efficacy of retatrutide in adults with overweight/obesity and CKD [estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 25-75 mL/min/1.73 m2], with and without T2D.

claims.claim: The mean age of the 146 participants randomized in the TRANSCEND-CKD trial was 65.1 years.
claims.quote: The mean age was 65.1 years [standard deviation (SD) 10.6], 45.2% were female and 69.9% were White.

claims.claim: Retatrutide is a triple receptor agonist targeting GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors.
claims.quote: Retatrutide, a novel triple receptor agonist targeting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide (GIP), and glucagon receptors, represents a groundbreaking advancement in obesity and T2DM pharmacotherapy.

claims.claim: Animal studies show retatrutide delays gastric emptying and reduces food intake.
claims.quote: Animal studies demonstrate retatrutide's ability to delay gastric emptying, reduce food intake, and promote weight loss, with superior efficacy compared to other incretin-based therapies.

claims.claim: Retatrutide has a mean half-life of approximately 6 days, supporting once-weekly dosing.
claims.quote: The pharmacokinetics of retatrutide were dose proportional and its mean half-life of approximately 6 days supported a once-weekly dosing.

claims.claim: Phase 1 and 2 clinical trials demonstrate retatrutide is associated with greater weight loss compared to placebo.
claims.quote: Each trial demonstrated greater weight loss with retatrutide treatment in comparison to placebo, with greatest efficacy at higher doses.

claims.claim: Retatrutide shows a robust intrinsic GIPR, GLP-1R, and GCGR potency hierarchy.
claims.quote: Retatrutide showed a highly robust intrinsic GIPR>GLP-1R>GCGR hierarchy, while its quantitative human activation vector remained underidentified.

claims.claim: Early clinical data suggest retatrutide may have hepatoprotective effects in MASLD.
claims.quote: Emerging agents like cotadutide (a GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist) and retatrutide (a GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triagonist) represent a novel therapeutic frontier, with early clinical data indicating potent hepatoprotective effects and favorable metabolic remodeling.

claims.claim: In US adults, the overall obesity prevalence increased from 46.7% to 61.7% between 1999 and 2018.
claims.quote: Overall obesity prevalence rose from 46.7% to 61.7%

claims.claim: Among US adults, clinical obesity was associated with a higher risk of all-cause mortality (HR 1.46) compared to preclinical obesity.
claims.quote: Clinical obesity was associated with significantly higher risks of all-cause (HR 1.46, 95% CI 1.29–1.66) and cardiovascular (HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.29–2.10) mortality versus preclinical obesity.

claims.claim: Combined overweight/obesity prevalence among midlife women in the US increased from 49.2% in 1990 to 74.2% in 2021.
claims.quote: Combined overweight/obesity prevalence increased from 49.2% (95% uncertainty interval (UI) 45.8-52.2; 17.7 million (95% UI 16.5-18.8 million)) in 1990 to 74.2% (95% UI 68.8-79.1; 33.4 million (95% UI 31.0-35.6 million)) in 2021

claims.claim: Among antiobesity medication users, 38.1% were classified as having pre-clinical obesity.
claims.quote: Of AOM users, 38.1% (n = 53,633) had pre-clinical obesity.

claims.claim: The age-standardized prevalence of clinical obesity in US adults increased from 14.3% in 1999-2000 to 26.6% in 2021-2023.
claims.quote: From 1999-2000 to 2021-2023, age-standardized prevalence of clinical obesity nearly doubled (14.3% to 26.6%; p < 0.001).

claims.claim: In the United States, the prevalence of adult obesity was 40.3% during the 2021-2023 period.
claims.quote: prevalence falling to 40.3% in 2021-2023

claims.claim: In 2021, the mean overweight/obesity prevalence across 50 US jurisdictions was 67.72%.
claims.quote: Across 50 US jurisdictions, including DC, the mean O/OV prevalence was 67.72%

claims.claim: In a study of US adults, higher serum DHA levels were associated with lower odds of central obesity in a cross-sectional analysis.
claims.quote: DHA was significantly associated with lower odds of central obesity (OR: 0·83, 95 % CI: 0·73-0·95)

claims.claim: In 2021, high BMI globally contributed to 5255 thyroid cancer-related deaths.
claims.quote: In 2021, high BMI contributed to 5255 thyroid cancer-related deaths

claims.claim: The overall prevalence of clinical obesity in US adults was 9.7% based on NHANES 2017-2020 data.
claims.quote: Among 8037 participants, the overall prevalence of clinical obesity was 9.7% (95% CI, 8.9%-10.5%), with comparable prevalence in males (9.8%) and in females (9.6%).
